question: Why does rate remain below 1 after correcting UE receiver noise bias?

confirmed.receiver_repair: Separate patch estimates noise from local pilot residuals rather than wideband coherent channel variation. Original UE archive changed only dmrs_sch.c.o; default original binary preserved.
confirmed.noise_validation: 10 trials × 400 frozen channels at 0/10/20/30 dB; candidate mean estimated/true noise ratio 0.9986–1.00075 for multipath. At 30 dB original ratio is 58.42, candidate 1.00047. Type1 frozen scenario is validated; general type2/multi-cell envelopes are not established.
confirmed.scheduler_event: UE ZMQ IO was woken by WORKER0 but waited runnable for 5.664 ms on CPU17. STACK at internal priority5 occupied CPU17 for 5.553 ms; IO was SCHED_OTHER. The event was captured in an instrumented run and is not retroactively assigned to earlier runs.
confirmed.priority_intervention: Only UE ZMQ IO policy changed SCHED_OTHER/0 -> SCHED_FIFO/95, on the same CPU17; WORKER and SYNC remain above it. No extra CPU core or ZMQ format changes.

why_not_exactly_one: Neither receiver repair nor UE IO priority removes every stall. Pacing rebases lateness beyond its 1 ms catch-up bound, retaining that wall-clock loss; finite measurement endpoints add a smaller phase difference. The sparse repeat reconciles most of its remaining loss with measured rebases, so the deficit cannot be dismissed as rounding.

remaining_repeat_event.description: Producer for gNB0 waited for output-buffer room. This proves the output was not drained in time, but does not by itself distinguish a late gNB request from delayed broker REP service. That initiating operation remains unresolved.

limits: The corrected estimator is an isolated candidate and is not enabled in the original/default UE binary.
Priority trials are individual runs with variable rare stalls, not proof of a guaranteed 1.000 rate or an expanded 8/16-UE scaling boundary.
Full scheduler captures noticeably perturb transport timing; they establish the specific runnable-starvation mechanism but do not measure the exact frequency of that event in uninstrumented runs.
No source-level attribution of the 5.553 ms STACK execution to one MAC/RLC operation has been established.
The remaining output-room event is not labeled a solved upstream cause.
